title: Clearing a boundary-supported fraction and its inverse in a normal domain
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal commutative domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and let $I$ be a finite set indexing distinct height-one prime ideals $\mathfrak p_i$ of $R$. For every height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ write $v_{\mathfrak q}:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for the normalized additive valuation of the discrete valuation ring $R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. A height-one prime is nonzero with no prime strictly between it and $(0)$. Suppose $\tau\in R\setminus\{0\}$ satisfies $v_{\mathfrak p_i}(\tau)>0$ for every $i\in I$ and $v_{\mathfrak q}(\tau)=0$ for every height-one prime not in this list. If $f\in K^\times$ satisfies $v_{\mathfrak q}(f)=0$ for every height-one prime outside the list, then there exist integers $N,H\ge0$ such that $h=f\tau^N$ and $h'=f^{-1}\tau^H$ both belong to $R$, and $hh'=\tau^{N+H}$ in $R$. More precisely, every $N,H\ge0$ satisfying $v_{\mathfrak p_i}(f)+Nv_{\mathfrak p_i}(\tau)\ge0$ and $-v_{\mathfrak p_i}(f)+Hv_{\mathfrak p_i}(\tau)\ge0$ for all $i$ has this property. The empty set $I$ is allowed.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), 031S (lemma-criterion-normal), and 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1); agent-formulated simultaneous valuation-clearing consequence, extracted from original steps 7--8 of lem-trf-complete-toric-boundary-class-injectivity.

proof.text: Write $a_i=v_{\mathfrak p_i}(f)$ and $b_i=v_{\mathfrak p_i}(\tau)$. Since $b_i$ is a positive integer, $b_i\ge1$. Set $N_0=\max(\{0\}\cup\{-a_i:i\in I\})$ and $H_0=\max(\{0\}\cup\{a_i:i\in I\})$. These maxima exist because $I$ is finite, including when it is empty. Then $a_i+N_0b_i\ge a_i+N_0\ge0$ and $-a_i+H_0b_i\ge-a_i+H_0\ge0$. Thus admissible nonnegative exponents exist. It remains to prove the asserted property for any admissible $N,H$.

source.place: Tag 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1), clause (2), with the explicit valuation-clearing argument supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Fix any such $N,H$ and put $h=f\tau^N$, $h\prime=f^{-1}\tau^H$ in $K^\times$. An additive valuation satisfies $v(xy)=v(x)+v(y)$, hence $v(x^{-1})=-v(x)$ and $v(x^n)=nv(x)$ by induction. At $\mathfrak p_i$ these formulas give the two assumed nonnegative integers. At every other height-one prime both valuations are zero by the support hypotheses. The DVR and membership assertions of [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel] therefore put both $h$ and $h\prime$ in every $R_{\mathfrak q}$. All hypotheses of that node hold: $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain and these are its height-one primes.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), normalized valuation; applied to the given height-one localizations.

proof.text: For each $g\in\{h,h\prime\}$ write $g=a/b$ with $a,b\in R$, $b\ne0$. Every associated prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R/bR$ has height one by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height]. Since $g\in R_{\mathfrak q}$, the fraction definition [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] writes $a/b=c/s$ with $c\in R$ and $s\notin\mathfrak q$. Cross multiplication in $K$, and the injective inclusion $R\subset K$, give $sa=bc$. Thus $s$ annihilates the class $\bar a\in R/bR$. The equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes], applied to the Noetherian ring $R$ and the module $R/bR$, gives $\bar a=0$. Hence $a=br$ for some $r\in R$, so $g=r\in R$. The same argument covers an empty set of associated primes because the cited statement explicitly allows the empty product.

source.place: Tag 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1), proof of (2) from (1), using Tag 0311 (lemma-zero-at-ass-zero).

proof.text: In $K$ cancellation gives $hh\prime=(f\tau^N)(f^{-1}\tau^H)=\tau^{N+H}$. All factors now lie in $R$ and $R\to K$ is injective, so the equality holds in $R$. This proves the claim for every admissible pair and hence for the explicit pair of step 1. If $I$ is empty, $N_0=H_0=0$ and the argument says directly that $f,f^{-1}\in R$ and their product is $1$.

The delivery is one commit with the item JSON and the report, and has no new nodes. The statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged, and the base proof was empty, so this is not a re-split. Step 1 picks exponents N0=max(0,-a_i) and H0=max(0,a_i), which works because b_i>=1 and also covers I empty. Step 2: the two valuations are >=0 at each p_i and 0 off the list, so the membership criterion of lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel (Noetherian normal domain, height-one primes, matching this item) puts h and h' in every R_q. Step 3 is exactly the proof of 031T(2): associated primes of R/bR have height one (pbc 031T(1) node), then sa=bc gives s·ā=0, then the 0311 node gives ā=0. A unit b leaves no associated primes, which that node allows. Step 4 is cancellation plus injectivity of R into K. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and a BFS shows no cycle. The two pbc tool_uses are declared and are the same pair accepted in the sibling divisor-kernel step 6; I accept them. Duplicates checked: krull-normalization would also give step 3 but is much heavier; divisor-kernel covers only div=0; the S2 total-fraction node is a different statement. None duplicates the item. Edge cases checked: R a field, k[x] with f=x^{-3}, the cone xy=z^2 with tau=x (off-list valuations correctly exclude z/x), and non-minimal exponents. No SGA is cited. The citer boundary-class-injectivity step 3 uses the item's statement, which is unchanged. One cosmetic point: the report lists sandbox-only files that are not in the delivery.
